I am 68 years old this year. I have been farming these fields since I was 23. My father taught me, and now my son works in the factory in town, so I still manage the 13.1 mu myself with help from my wife at busy times. I only finished primary school, but I know these fields like the back of my hand. I watch what my neighbors do, and I mostly do what I did last year because changing things is dangerous.

**My wheat this year:**

I grow wheat on all 13.1 mu in the winter season. I will sow Jimai 22 — it is an improved variety that my neighbor Lao Zhang has been using for several years, and he always gets a good harvest. Last year I used the same seed, and I got about 1000 jin per mu, so I will stick with it. I sow about 30 jin of seed per mu.

For fertilizer, I learned long ago that wheat needs a good base. I will put down 100 jin per mu of compound fertilizer at sowing — the bag says 18-22-8, I buy it from the dealer in town. That is my basal dressing. Then in the spring, when the wheat is at jointing stage and I can see it turning green strong, I will topdress with 50 jin per mu of urea. I would rather put a little too much than too little. A bad wheat harvest means I have no money for the whole year; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost I can bear. I do not buy straight phosphate or potash — the compound bag has enough.

Irrigation costs money because I pump from my well, but wheat cannot dry out. I will irrigate four times: once after sowing if it is dry, once in winter if there is no snow, once at jointing, and once at flowering. My neighbors all irrigate three or four times, so I do four to be safe.

For pests, I spray herbicide once in early spring to kill the weeds. I spray insecticide twice — once when the aphids come, and once more if I see damage. I do not usually spray fungicide unless the neighbors say rust is spreading. So that is three sprays in total.

I till with rotary tillage before sowing wheat. The machine goes through after the maize stalks are chopped.

I expect 500 kg per mu if the weather is normal, maybe a bit more if spring rain is good.

**My maize this year:**

After the wheat comes off in June, I sow maize on the same 13.1 mu. I use hybrid seed — Denghai 605 or Zhengdan 958, whatever the dealer has in stock. I need about 1.5 kg of seed per mu. I sow directly into the wheat stubble without tilling — no-tillage. Everyone around here does it this way now. It saves time and diesel, and the maize grows fine if you get the seed in the ground quick after harvest.

For fertilizer, I put 80 jin per mu of compound fertilizer at sowing — the dealer gives me the high-nitrogen kind, 28-6-6, because maize needs nitrogen. I do not usually topdress maize with urea. My neighbors mostly do the same, and we get good ears. Some young people talk about extra urea at the big trumpet stage, but I have tried it and I did not see enough difference to pay for it.

Maize needs less water than wheat. I irrigate twice: once right after sowing to help it germinate, and once at the big trumpet stage if the rain does not come. Last year I only irrigated once and still got over 1000 jin per mu.

For sprays, I put herbicide down once at sowing to stop weeds. I spray insecticide twice for the corn borer — those worms can ruin the whole crop if you let them. That is three sprays total.

I expect about 520 kg per mu from the maize if the autumn weather is decent.

**Why I do it this way:**

My son sends some money home from his factory job, but the farm still has to pay for itself. I watch every yuan. Fertilizer is expensive now, but going short is worse — I remember 2009 when I tried to save on urea and the wheat was thin as grass. I lost more than I saved. So I follow what worked last year, I watch my neighbors, and I do not take risks on new ideas unless I see them work on someone else's field first. With 13.1 mu, I am not the biggest farmer in the village, but I am not the smallest either. I can afford the inputs I need, but I cannot afford a failed crop.
